input_payload: Customer disputes INR 15,000 hotel booking chargeback: claims service not rendered (hotel was closed on travel date). Should we contest?
evidence_pool: Hotel 'Sunrise Palace, Goa' — confirmed closure notice posted on their website on travel date (14 Aug).
Customer notified of closure by hotel via email on 12 Aug; email read receipt confirmed.
Merchant offered alternate dates; customer declined and requested full refund.
Refund was not processed by merchant prior to chargeback filing.
Merchant cancellation policy: full refund for hotel-initiated cancellations.
ground_truth: Accept: hotel-initiated cancellation entitles customer to full refund per merchant's own policy. Contesting this dispute would likely fail and damage reputation.

input_payload: Chargeback: customer claims INR 4,500 subscription charge is unauthorized — they cancelled the subscription 30 days ago. Merchant has no cancellation record. Contest or accept?
evidence_pool: Merchant's subscription management system: no cancellation request logged for customer ID CUS-3341.
Customer's email: cancellation request sent to 'support@merchant-old-domain.com' (deprecated address, not monitored).
Customer has screenshots of confirmation email from deprecated support address.
Active subscription debit continued for 3 months after customer's attempted cancellation.
Consumer Protection Act 2019: merchants must process cancellations from all reasonable contact channels.
ground_truth: Accept: customer made cancellation attempt in good faith; deprecated email oversight is merchant's responsibility under consumer protection rules. Refund all 3 post-cancellation charges.
